Folks — technical notes from the runtime team:

1) Current pool: 200 usable A100-equivalent slots across the west-coast fleet during the May window. After baseline commitments, ~92 GPUs are unallocated but not all are in the same availability zone.
2) Cold-starts + model KV cache: CanyonHealths profile indicates heavy seq-len and large KV working set. That means theyll occupy nodes for longer duty cycles per request; effective throughput is ~10-15% lower than the average model.
3) Operational friction: frequent VPC attachments and VLANs for two large customers in the same AZ increases blast radius risk.

Given the constraints, the safe production plan:
- Reserve 64 GPUs for CanyonHealth in AZ-us-west-2a with a 6-week hard commitment.
- Offer NebulaAI 28 GPUs reserved in us-west-2b + an automated burst policy to borrow up to 24 GPUs across AZs when cross-AZ bandwidth permits.
- Enable prefetched KV caching and prewarm scripts for Canyon to reduce per-request latency during the first 48 hours.

Operational caveat: this leaves ~0-40 unreserved GPUs for ad-hoc requests during peak days depending on cross-AZ burst. Well need approval for a temporary burst-capacity budget (estimated cost delta ~$28k/week) or negotiate credits with NebulaAI.

—Markus
